bioParagraphs: I started with the MERN stack because I wanted to understand how products were built from end to end — the interface, the APIs, the database, and everything connecting them.
My first internship changed the way I thought about software.

Working with a production codebase taught me things that tutorials couldn't: how to structure code so it can change safely, how APIs behave under real traffic, how asynchronous workflows fail, and how small architectural decisions become expensive when a system grows.
That's what pulled me deeper into backend engineering.

At EY, I worked on an EPFO WhatsApp engagement platform that scaled to 1M+ active campaign users. I worked across APIs, webhooks, Redis Streams, asynchronous processing, microservices, idempotency, and the systems behind large-scale messaging workflows.

At Mednex, I worked on an autonomous GTM AI platform, building agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, list-building systems, background jobs, and the backend infrastructure connecting them. The interesting part wasn't just making an LLM produce an answer — it was making the entire workflow behave reliably when real data, external services, and long-running jobs entered the picture.
That's the kind of engineering I enjoy.

I like taking an ambiguous problem, breaking it down into systems, and making those systems simpler, faster, and more reliable. Sometimes that means designing an API. Sometimes it means rethinking a queue, eliminating a bottleneck, or figuring out how an AI workflow should recover when something fails.
I'm particularly interested in scalability, performance optimization, reliable backend systems, distributed workflows, and AI-powered products.
I still enjoy building across the stack — but I'm increasingly drawn to the engineering underneath the product: the part that makes everything else work.

projects.title: ToolTap
projects.description: A backend-first AI agent that turns WhatsApp into a full tool-calling interface. The interesting part isn't the chat UI — it's the orchestration underneath: async webhook processing, tool-calling loops, and graceful failure when the LLM or a tool times out mid-conversation.

projects.title: WarmTalk
projects.description: A full-stack, HIPAA-minded mental health platform built with Next.js, Node.js, and PostgreSQL. Real-time secure messaging (Socket.io), inclusive therapist matching, and integrated video consultations — therapy that feels like home.
